case_title: G. RAMESH v. KANIKE HARISH KUMAR UJWAL & ANR.
accused_occupation: Partnership firm dealing in data entry
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused, a partnership firm, obtained contracts for data entry work and subcontracted the work to the complainant. The complainant was paid a caution deposit and completed the data entry work. The accused issued cheques for the payment, which were dishonoured due to insufficient funds. The accused assured the complainant that the cheques would be honoured on re-presentation. The complainant presented the cheques again, but they were returned unpaid. The complainant issued a notice of demand for payment, which was not fulfilled. The complainant filed a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. The High Court quashed the complaint, but the Supreme Court allowed the appeal, finding that the complaint contained sufficient averments to meet the requirements of Section 141.
